name: Theudas
description: Man living at the time of the New Testament

points: These two men he mentions, Theudas and Judas of Galilee: they set themselves up to be somebody, and they got put to death, because both of their intent was to go against the laws of the land, and all, as many as obeyed them, were dispersed.

note.label: Living Your Life As A Hireling

points: Gamaliel, a doctor of the law, had in reputation among all the people, told the council: before these days rose up Theudas, boasting himself to be somebody, and all that obeyed him were scattered and brought to nought. After him rose up Judas of Galilee, and he also perished. We have that today: brothers come to the body, learn the scriptures a little bit, then go forth and heap men unto themselves, and when they leave, the men come to nought.

Gamaliel warns the council to take heed what they do: before these days Theudas rose up boasting himself to be somebody, and about four hundred joined him, but he was slain and his followers scattered to nothing; after him Judas of Galilee drew people in the days of the taxing and also perished, and his followers were dispersed.

The record of Josephus tells the same of Theudas, a magician who persuaded a great part of the people that he was a prophet who could divide the river Jordan, until horsemen fell on them, killed many, and beheaded him; examine such men and see what their work comes to.

note.label: Acts 5: All Things Common, and We Ought to Obey God Rather Than Men
